reasoning_traces.think:
The DID estimator captures average treatment effects by comparing changes in outcomes between treated and control groups over time. It assumes parallel trends in the absence of treatment. The SCM method constructs a synthetic control by weighting donors to approximate the pre-intervention trajectory of the treated unit. Both methods complement each other: DID provides a global estimate while SCM offers individualized counterfactuals. The dual approach enhances robustness through multiple identification strategies. Failure modes include violation of parallel trends in DID and poor donor selection in SCM. Placebo testing ensures validity by confirming that spurious effects do not emerge under known null conditions.
